'''Jared Anthony Dudley''' (born July 10, 1985) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach for the [[Denver Nuggets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[Forward (basketball)|forward]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College Eagles]].

Dudley was selected with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]]. After a season and a half in Charlotte, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in December 2008. He would spend five seasons with the team before being dealt to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in July 2013. In August 2014, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. In July 2015, Dudley was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]]. He made a return to Phoenix in July 2016 and spent another two years with the franchise before being traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in July 2018. In July 2019, he signed a one-year deal with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Dudley won an [[NBA championship]] with the Lakers in 2020. He re-signed with the Lakers in November 2020 before retiring in August 2021 and joining the Mavericks' coaching staff. In July 2025 he accepted an offer to become the top assistant coach for the [[Denver Nuggets]].

==College career==
During his college years, Dudley played with the [[Boston College]] [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Eagles]]. During the 2004–05 season, he earned the nickname "'''Junkyard Dog'''" for his toughness and nose for the ball.

He scored 30 points on November 29, 2006, against [[Michigan State University|Michigan State]] on national television.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121010001925/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=263330103 BC tops MSU behind 30 points, 10 boards from Dudley]</ref> His career-high in points is 36, which he scored against [[Villanova University|Villanova]] in a January 19, 2005 victory during his sophomore season.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2005/02/24/sports/ncaabasketball/24villanova.html Villanova Is Getting Hot When It Counts Most]</ref> He averaged 19 points and 3 assists per game during his senior year.

After his senior season, Dudley was voted the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] for 2007 and was a second team [[All-American]].

==Professional career==

===Charlotte Bobcats (2007–2008)===
On June 28, 2007, Dudley was taken 22nd overall in the [[2007 NBA Draft|NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].

Soon after the 2007 draft, Dudley entered the Bobcats' regular playing rotation and made his first start on November 24, 2007, vs. [[Boston Celtics|Boston]], scoring 11 points and grabbing nine rebounds.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=271124030 | title=Celtics 96, Bobcats 95 | work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>  He went on to establish himself as a key player in the Bobcats' rotation, starting often while with the team. He finished the 2007–08 season averaging 5.8 points a game. He also played as the team's power forward during his rookie season with the Bobcats before being more of a small forward in his second season with them.

Dudley played 20 games for the Bobcats in 2008 before he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. In those 20 games, he averaged what would be a career low 5.4 points.

===Phoenix Suns (2008–2013)===
[[file:Jared Dudley Suns.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Dudley with the Suns in 2011]]
Dudley was traded to the Suns on December 18, 2008, along with teammate [[Jason Richardson]] and [[Gani Lawal|the Bobcats' 2010 second round pick]], in exchange for [[Raja Bell]], [[Boris Diaw]], and [[Sean Singletary]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suns Trade for Richardson, Dudley and 2010 Second-Round Pick |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/trade_081210.html |access-date=2008-12-11}}</ref> He gained media attention for posting journalist-style videos of interviews with his Suns teammates on [[Twitter]] under the name of JMZ or JSPN (parodies of [[TMZ.com]] and [[ESPN]] respectively).<ref>azcentral.com (2010). [https://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2010/04/01/20100401phoenix-suns-jared-dudley-twitter.html Phoenix Suns' Jared Dudley gains followers with Twitter videos]. Retrieved April 18, 2010.</ref> Dudley played in 48 games for the Suns that season and averaged 3.0 rebounds per game, 0.8 assists a game, and 5.5 points per game.

In the 2009–10 season Dudley was a key player in the [[2010 NBA Playoffs]]. He played in all of the Suns 16 playoff games that season, shooting 42.4% on three-pointers. But the Suns eventually lost to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the Western Conference Finals by a margin of four games to two.

Although the Suns failed to reach the playoffs in the 2010–11 season, Dudley averaged a career-high 10.6 points per game. He once again played in all 82 games and started a career-high 15 of them.

In the shortened 2011–12 season, Dudley increased his career high with 12.7 points while also averaging a career-high 4.6 rebounds and career-high 1.7 assists per game while starting for the Suns in 60 of their games as a shooting guard instead of a small forward. However, the Suns missed the playoffs once again. After the [[2011–12 NBA season]], [[NBA TV]] announced that Dudley was the first ever winner of the "BIG Award",<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/features/07/09/2012-social-media-awards/index.html |title=2011-12 Social Media Award Winners |work=NBA.com |date=July 12, 2012 |access-date=July 18, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120713121858/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/features/07/09/2012-social-media-awards/index.html |archive-date=July 13, 2012 }}</ref> beating out the likes of [[James Harden]] and [[Kevin Love]] due to his use of social media websites like [[Twitter]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/video/channels/nba_tv/2012/06/20/sma2012_big_award_dudley.nba/index.html |title=The Big Award |work=NBA.com |date=July 12, 2012 |access-date=July 18, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120622055232/http://www.nba.com/video/channels/nba_tv/2012/06/20/sma2012_big_award_dudley.nba/index.html |archive-date=June 22, 2012 }}</ref>

Due to the departure of veterans [[Steve Nash]] and [[Grant Hill]], Dudley and [[Jermaine O'Neal]] were named the Suns' captains for the [[2012–13 NBA season]]. On December 27, 2012, Dudley recorded a career-high 36 points on 11-of-17 shooting (5-of-8 from the three-point line and a perfect 9-of-9 from the free throw line), as well as five rebounds and three assists against the [[New York Knicks]].

===Los Angeles Clippers (2013–2014)===
On July 10, 2013, Dudley was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in a three-team deal that also included the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] getting draft picks and [[Phoenix Suns]] getting players in exchange, primarily [[Eric Bledsoe]].<ref>{{cite web|title=CLIPPERS ACQUIRE JARED DUDLEY AND J.J. REDICK IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-redickdudley-130710|work=NBA.com|access-date=10 July 2013}}</ref> Dudley was the Clippers' starting small forward until January 20, 2014, when he was replaced by [[Matt Barnes]].

===Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2015)===
On August 26, 2014, Dudley was traded, along with a 2017 conditional first round draft pick, to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Carlos Delfino]], [[Miroslav Raduljica]] and a 2015 second round draft pick.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-jared-dudley-clippers Bucks Acquire Jared Dudley and First Round Pick From Clippers]</ref> He would play as the team's shooting guard that season due to Milwaukee's size at the frontcourt. On December 26, 2014, Dudley became the first player to shoot 100% from the field for an entire game with at least 10 overall shots and 3 three-point shots by making 10-of-10 field goals and 4-of-4 shots from the three-point line as he recorded 24 points, 4 rebounds, 4 steals and 2 assists off the bench in a blowout 107–77 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141226/MILATL/gameinfo.html |title=Perfect 10: Dudley doesn't miss, Bucks rout Hawks |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228180441/http://www.nba.com/games/20141226/MILATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2014-12-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On June 30, 2015, Dudley opted in with the Bucks for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/06/30/bucks-dudley/index.html|title=Report: Jared Dudley opting in with Bucks next season|date=June 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 30, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/sports/bucks/bucks-jared-dudley-opts-in-for-final-year-of-deal-b99529558z1-311104021.html|title=Bucks' Jared Dudley opts in for final year of deal|date=June 30, 2015|work=JournalSentinelOnline.com|access-date=July 6, 2015}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2015–2016)===
On July 9, 2015, Dudley was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for a protected future second round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/07/09/wizards-acquire-jared-dudley|title=WIZARDS ACQUIRE JARED DUDLEY|access-date=July 9, 2015|date=July 9, 2015|work=MonumentalNetwork.com}}</ref> On July 21, he was ruled out for three to four months after undergoing surgery to repair a herniated disk.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13297878/jared-dudley-washington-wizards-3-4-months-back-surgery|title=Jared Dudley out 3 to 4 months after surgery to fix herniated disk|access-date=July 23, 2015|date=July 21, 2015|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Dudley spent much of the 2015–16 season as the team's power forward, due to the Wizards' lack of size at that position.{{citation needed|date=February 2023}}

===Return to Phoenix (2016–2018)===
On July 8, 2016, Dudley signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-jared-dudley-multiyear-deal|title=Suns Sign Jared Dudley to Multiyear Deal|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> While not his primary position, Dudley was made the Suns' power forward to start the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]].<ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/10/03/phoenix-suns-brandon-knight-come-off-bench/91489330/ Phoenix Suns' Brandon Knight will come off the bench]</ref> He was moved to the bench after seven games, and on November 9, he scored a season-high 19 points off the bench in a 107–100 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899563|title=Bledsoe, Dudley lead Suns past Pistons 105-99 [sic]|work=ESPN.com|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}}</ref> On March 24, 2017, he recorded a season-high 10 assists in a 130–120 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]. On April 5, he scored a season high-tying 19 points in a 120–111 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dudleja01/gamelog/2017/|title=Jared Dudley 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 8, 2017}}</ref>

On June 23, 2017, Dudley underwent a left toe ligament and bone procedure, ruling him out for three to four months.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cunningham|first=Cody|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-forward-jared-dudley-underwent-surgery|title=Suns Forward Jared Dudley Underwent Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2017|access-date=July 3, 2017}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019)===
On July 20, 2018, Dudley and a protected 2021 second round draft pick were traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Darrell Arthur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/20/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-phoenix-suns|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Phoenix Suns|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2018|access-date=July 20, 2018}}</ref> He missed 16 games over January and February of the 2018–19 season with a strained left hamstring.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071542|title=Center duo of Nurkic, Kanter leads Blazers over Nets, 113-99|work=ESPN.com|date=February 21, 2019|access-date=February 22, 2019}}</ref> During Round 1 of the [[2019 NBA Playoffs]], he got into a feud with [[Philadelphia 76ers]] player [[Ben Simmons]]. He also got into an altercation with other 76ers players. Dudley was fined $25,000 for the incident.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sixers' Jimmy Butler, Nets' Jared Dudley fined after Game 4 melee|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-nets-fines-jimmy-butler-jared-dudley-sean-marks-joel-embiid-20190421.html|access-date=October 10, 2021|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=21 April 2019 }}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2021)===
On July 7, 2019, Dudley signed a one-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for $2.6 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190707-lakers-sign-daniels-dudley|title=Lakers Sign Troy Daniels and Jared Dudley|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Lakers to add F Dudley on 1-year, $2.6M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27107717/lakers-add-f-dudley-1-year-26m-deal|access-date=October 30, 2021|website=ESPN|date=3 July 2019 }}</ref> On August 13, 2020, he logged a season-high five assists in a 122–136 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings vs Los Angeles Lakers Aug 13, 2020 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021901310 |access-date=November 21, 2021 |website=NBA}}</ref> On December 11, he was ejected from a game against the [[Orlando Magic]] after an on-court fight involving players from both teams. Teammate [[LeBron James]] later praised Dudley's actions, stating, "I've seen a lot more than that. But 'Dudz' will do whatever. He told you guys at media day his job is to come in here if somebody goes crazy, do something crazy to me or [[Anthony Davis|AD]] or whoever on the team, he's going to be the muscle." Dudley recorded a season-high nine points and three rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lakers question Jared Dudley's quick ejection, laud his actions vs. Magic |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28280259/lakers-question-jared-dudley-quick-ejection-laud-actions-vs-magic |access-date=October 30, 2021 |website=ESPN|date=12 December 2019 }}</ref> Dudley won his only NBA championship as a player when the Lakers defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in six games in the [[2020 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers are the 2020 NBA Champions|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/champions-2020|access-date=October 30, 2021|website=Los Angeles Lakers}}</ref>

On November 30, 2020, Dudley re-signed with the Lakers on another 1-year, $2.6 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jared Dudley returning to Los Angeles Lakers on 1-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30424134/jared-dudley-returning-los-angeles-lakers-1-year-deal|access-date=October 30, 2021|website=ESPN|date=December 2020 }}</ref> On December 27, he scored a season-high 3 points along with two rebounds in a 127–91 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves vs Los Angeles Lakers Dec 27, 2020 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000040|access-date=November 21, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> He matched this total on February 24, 2021, along with four rebounds and an assist in an 89–114 blowout loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Utah Jazz Feb 24, 2021 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000497|access-date=November 21, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On March 3, Dudley grabbed a season-high two assists in a 120–123 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Sacramento Kings Mar 3, 2021 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000551|access-date=November 21, 2021|website=NBA}}</ref> On March 14, the Lakers announced that Dudley had suffered a contusion and torn MCL in his right knee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lakers' Jared Dudley tears ligament in right knee |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2021-03-14/lakers-jared-dudley-tears-mcl-in-right-knee |access-date=March 14, 2022 |website=The Los Angeles Times|date=15 March 2021 }}</ref> However, he opted to not undergo surgery on his knee and instead underwent a period of rehab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lakers' Jared Dudley says he'll return from torn MCL before playoffs begin |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/lakers-jared-dudley-says-hell-return-from-torn-mcl-before-playoffs-begin/ |access-date=March 14, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=7 May 2021 }}</ref> He made his return from injury on May 16, 2021, after missing 33 games, playing four minutes in a 110–98 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs New Orleans Pelicans May 16, 2021 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022001072 |access-date=March 14, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref>

At the conclusion of the 2020-21 season, Dudley announced his retirement from the NBA after 14 seasons.

==Coaching career==
===Dallas Mavericks (2021–2025)===
On August 24, 2021, Dudley joined [[Jason Kidd]]'s coaching staff with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as an assistant coach. Dudley was expected to have a "front of the bench" role with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rader|first=Doyle|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/doylerader/2021/08/25/jared-dudley-joining-dallas-mavericks-as-an-assistant-coach/?sh=5472bd3e665e|title=Jared Dudley Joining Dallas Mavericks As An Assistant Coach|work=Forbes|date=August 25, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2025–present)===
On July 3, 2025, [[Shams Charania]] reported that Dudley was joining the [[Denver Nuggets]] as their top assistant coach under [[David Adelman (basketball)|David Adelman]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gross |first=Gordon |date=2025-07-03 |title=Breaking: Denver Nuggets to add Jared Dudley as top assistant |url=https://www.denverstiffs.com/breaking-denver-nuggets-to-add-jared-dudley-as-top-assistant/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=Denver Stiffs |language=en}}</ref>

Romans 6:8-11}}</ref> He appeared in the comedy film ''[[Movie 43]]'' (2013), as a basketball player named Moses.<ref>[http://valleyofthesuns.com/2012/10/05/jared-dudley-is-the-new-era-phoenix-suns-big-bang/ Jared Dudley is the new era Phoenix Suns' Big Bang]</ref> Fellow NBA players [[Corey Brewer]] and [[Larry Sanders (basketball)|Larry Sanders]] also appeared in the film. On February 2, 2021, Dudley and [[Carvell Wallace]] released a short, mostly autobiographical [[e-book]] called ''Inside the NBA Bubble: A Championship Season under Quarantine'' on [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]].<ref>[https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08T5SKBRW/ref=apubna_mq_na_30391_ul_1_1_2102 Amazon.com: Inside the NBA Bubble: A Championship Season under Quarantine eBook: Dudley, Jared, Wallace, Carvell: Kindle Store]</ref> His book talked about his personal experience, feelings, and the settings for the Lakers' 17th NBA Finals won inside the [[2020 NBA Bubble]] at [[Walt Disney World]]'s [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]].<ref>[https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2021/2/3/22264365/jared-dudley-lakers-clippers-beef-with-paul-george-book-nba-bubble-amazon-kindle Jared Dudley reveals the real reasons the Lakers had beef with Paul George, the Clippers in the bubble]</ref>
